extraction.agency_name: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene
extraction.parent_department: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene

findings.title: The Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists did not properly track complaints against licensees, resulting in complaints not being investigated and submitted to the Office of the Attorney General for administrative and/or criminal action in a timely manner.
findings.description: The Board did not properly track or monitor complaints related to 7,800 active licensees. Complaint logs contained incomplete information, leading to untimely investigation and submission to the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) for 9 of 15 tested complaints as of December 2016.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that the Board a. properly monitor complaints and develop a strategy to ensure timely disposition; b. ensure complaints are promptly referred to OAG upon recommendation for administrative action; c. properly maintain the tracking log.

findings.title: The Board of Nursing did not always take timely action to suspend the licenses of delinquent noncustodial parents referred by the Child Support Enforcement Administration as required by State law.
findings.description: Review disclosed that the Board did not always take timely action to suspend licenses. Of 236 referrals from July 2013 to November 2015, written notice of suspension was not sent for 88 referrals for periods ranging from one to five months after notification.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that the Board take timely action to suspend the licenses of delinquent noncustodial parents referred by CSEA as required by State law.

findings.title: The Office of Health Care Quality did not conduct annual inspections of certain health care facilities as required.
findings.description: OHCQ did not inspect certain health care facilities annually. For fiscal year 2015, OHCQ had not performed inspections for 308 of the 1,497 assisted living facilities and 132 of the 203 facilities for the developmentally disabled.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that OHCQ, in conjunction with DHMH, develop a strategy to ensure inspections of the various health care facilities are completed as required by law.

findings.title: The Maryland Medical Cannabis Commission improperly used interagency agreements with a State university to procure license application evaluation services, circumventing competitive procurement and control agency approvals.
findings.description: MMCC procured services through interagency agreements with Towson University's RESI, circumventing competitive procurement. Agreements were artificially split and understated, increasing value from $545,000 to $2.4 million. Overhead rates were not reviewed for reasonableness.

dollar_amounts.context: Modified agreement value and invoices received

findings.recommendation: We recommend that MMCC a. discontinue using interagency agreements to avoid competitive procurement; b. discontinue splitting contracts to circumvent oversight; c. ensure estimates and overhead rates are reasonable; d. approve RESI invoices for payment once documentation is received.

findings.title: Certain boards did not adequately control and account for collections.
findings.description: Four boards reviewed did not establish adequate controls. Board of Physicians had employees with access to both deposit verifications and mail-in collections; deposits were late totaling $68,800. Board of Nursing lacked segregation of duties and verification documentation. Board of Pharmacy deposits were late totaling $564,300.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that the applicable Boards a. ensure employees responsible for deposit verifications do not have access to collections; b. deposit collections within one working day of receipt; c. perform documented verifications of deposits; d. verify accuracy of credit card payment data; e. periodically reconcile licensing activity with collections.

findings.title: Seventeen boards and commissions did not ensure that employees who handled collections were denied the capability to issue or renew licenses in the electronic licensing systems.
findings.description: Seventeen of 20 boards reviewed allowed cash handling employees system user functions to issue or renew licenses. This created a risk that employees could misappropriate collections without detection.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that the boards and commissions a. ensure employees processing collections are denied system capability to issue or renew licenses; b. consider feasibility of using a bank lockbox account.

findings.title: The Board of Physicians did not adequately monitor a rehabilitation services vendor and did not always obtain documentation to support amounts invoiced.
findings.description: Board contracted with a vendor for $2.5 million but did not maintain documentation verifying services provided or compare plans with records. Test of two invoices totaling $237,500 disclosed one invoice lacked required quarterly detail reports prior to payment.

dollar_amounts.context: Payments for period January 1, 2015 through February 17, 2016

findings.recommendation: We recommend that the Board a. obtain and review supporting documentation to ensure appropriate rehabilitation services were provided; b. ensure quarterly detail reports are received for all program participants prior to invoice payment.

findings.title: Password and account controls for the Boards of Nursing, Physicians, and Pharmacy were not sufficient to properly protect critical data.
findings.description: Password and account controls did not comply with State Information Security Policy regarding length, complexity, age, history, and lockout. Settings were not enforced for production licensing databases used by the Boards.
findings.recommendation: We recommend that a. the three Boards implement strong controls over passwords and accounts; b. DHMH determine extent to which additional controls are needed for remaining boards.

extraction.agency_response_summary: The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene generally concurs with all audit recommendations. Agencies indicated that corrective actions were implemented or planned, including hiring additional staff, revising processes, and submitting reports by specific dates such as May 2017 and October 2017.
extraction.extraction_notes: Report date taken from transmittal letter. Audit period explicitly stated in text. Repeat findings identified by asterisk in TOC and 'repeat' tag in recommendations.
